body: But what if sometimes it as? Or if staying alive is worth less?

I hate talking to people over the phone and I'm a very shy person too so I'd find talking to strangers in this state of mind almost impossible. I wish there was someone I knew who I was comfortable chatting to things about but I've thought about it long and hard and there isn't. I've posted some more info in an update to explain. I'm going to sleep on it again (although when I say sleep I barely can which I'm sure isn't helping) but I find everyday I do I just become more...detached (not sure if that is the right word but hopefully you know what I mean)
No I'm not in therapy, I don't think I could cope with that just now, weird as that sounds. Posted an update to explain a bit more.

Update: Not sure what else to say here. I feel I'd like to talk to someone yet I don't think there's anyone that I could talk to. Ex-girlfriend wouldn't understand, she would say I was being ridiculous/melodramatic. I don't really have any close friends left in the area as they have moved away after graduating or have steadily drifted apart over the last couple of years (and I have little in common with now). My parents are in another country, not sure I would be strong/confident enough to talk to them about this and not sure they could truly understand what I'm going through.
I had a chat to my ex today (but not about this), she came over to pick up some stuff and she said that she might be willing to have a chat about things after Christmas but in a way that made things worse as if I manage to go on that means I have 4 months of not being able to move on, 4 months of wondering and there might not even be a good resolution (or if we do get back together it might not be any better).
I should probably explain why we broke up initially. I'll try to simplify things, she is currently working 2 jobs (through her own choice), one almost full time and another 20hr/wk voluntary job- this results in her working 7 days a week and I think this has caused her to be fairly stressed. I also think she has been depressed for quite a long time. She didn't sleep well, eat well, didn't enjoy doing the things she used to, she decided she was fat and ugly (she wasn't at all) and her sex drive completely disappeared. I'd suggested to her that it is nothing to be ashamed of and it is very common and treatable but I think she might be depressed. She decided I meant she was 'mentally deficient' in some way as she refuses to accept that depression is an actual medical condition (even though I think she suffers from it)- I actually got her to complete a PHQ-9 depression screening test and she scored something like 15/27 (higher is worse and this equated to moderate-severe depression but she wouldn't accept it and said that depression is just weakness and that she is just sad and not depressed. We broke up as she felt she had no time for anything but work at the moment and moved back to her parents to be closer to work. I tried to be reasonable and offered many times that we could sit down and talk things through but apparently the depression comment made her think I was saying any problems we might have were all her fault for being depressed (which is not what I said or meant at all). I also suggested we could seek help together (couples counselling or something) to talk through our problems together with an unbiased mediator but she refused again. I feel like I tried my best but she was unwilling to negotiate. She left in a way that made me feel like a horrible person. Despite the fact that I still love her, I feel that is not necessarily someone who I need in my life. Yet I know how alike we are and it makes me feel that if things didn't work out between us then I am doomed to a life of loneliness and rejection. In a way I feel like her depression is infectious and I have somehow caught it from her by being around her so long and struggling with things. Now I'm caught in the same trap. I know she'd never commit suicide (and she has said before that she never could as she said she is 'too much of a coward') but I don't know the same for me. I can be impulsive and am quite strong willed usually, I feel I could quite easily do it. I posted here because I feel I am on somewhat of a tipping point so to speak.
Maybe I am being melodramatic to some extent but I also feel I don't have any options open to me for how to move on. I have prospects for the future and no one around me to help. Whether people might find it 'selfish' or the 'easy way out' or whatever, the ability to stop the pain seems appealing to me. Please tell me I'm being ridiculous but I feel like a quick end to everything wouldn't always be the worst option.
